/** *

Gets a debugging string version of this formatter.

ownership_reason: Only the scan in copyWordStarts sees the individual characters and decides where a word starts; every caller sees only the copied characters and their count. Once the scan stops leaving a word at whitespace it copies the first character of the first word and nothing else, so the starts of the later words are gone: no caller can rebuild them from 'B' and a count of 1, and no pre-filtering of the input lets one scan report several word starts. The same convention (a whitespace character ends the current word, the next non-whitespace character starts one) is carried by the sibling overload initials(String, char[]) with null delimiters (lastWasGap = true at every whitespace), by capitalize/uncapitalize (capitalizeNext/uncapitalizeNext = true at every delimiter) and by swapCase; testInitials_String_charArray's null block (BJL, BJ, BJ.L, iah1) pins it through the intact overload. Known bypasses (W13, not competing repairs): the facade restoring `return initials(str, null);` or hop 1 returning WordUtils.initials(str, null), each discarding the chain.
